new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (4 pp., text layer present; the PDF's metadata gives the Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-09-20; p.1 header 'Organised Phonology Data / Yagwoia Language [YGW] / Menyamya - Morobe Province.. Major villages: Kwaplalim, Hekwange, Tsewi.. Data checked by: Mike Trainum (July 1992)'). At the stated locator, p.3 lines 30-33 of the extracted text layout read exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) / Tone is phonemic but has a low functional load: / hyékuyi 'bad betelnut' qalyí 'lightweight' / hyekúye 'death adder' qálye 'plant sp.''; p.4 line 4 under 'Conventions: Orthographic' reads 'Tone is not.' The reader's quote is verbatim in wording; the only differences are editorial (s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand prosodic statement: Yagwoia has phonemic 'tone' of low functional load, illustrated by pairs differing in which syllable carries the (acute-marked) high pitch; the source says nothing about where stress falls, whether stress exists independently, or vowel length. The examples look like a culminative accent contrast (one marked syllable per word, position lexical), but the source labels it tone and gives no placement rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms (isolated lexical minimal pairs). Lloyd 1973: 87 adds only a family-level remark for Angan: 'Tone and stress are combined in a complex unit which usually occurs in connection with the grammatical stem', with non-Angaataha Angan languages characterised as 'more intonation languages'; his Yagwoia section (pp. 53-55) is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes Yagwoia as spoken around Kwaplalim, Hekwange and Tsewi (Menyamya District, Morobe) = yagw1240 proper. Lloyd 1973's sketch rests on Weier & Grieger 1960 (Menyamya area); Fischer 1968 describes the northern Yeghuye/Jeghuje ('Yaguya') dialect group. Glottolog lists no dialect glottocodes under yagw1240.
